content:
The transaction system provides a "dry run" mode to allow validating transaction parameters without committing changes to the database. However, transactions triggered via standard user channels are being permanently written to the database even when dry run is requested.
Investigate the propagation of execution options, find where the dry run flag is being lost, and fix it.
Ensure that non-dry run transactions continue to be written to the database.

<result>I have now traced the complete call chain for the dry-run bug. Here is the full investigation report.

## 1. Definition of the options struct with the dry-run flag

**File:** `src/model/transaction.h` (lines 6-18)

```cpp
struct Transaction {
    std::string id;
    double amount;
};

struct TransactionOptions {
    bool dry_run = false;
    bool bypass_cache = false;

    static TransactionOptions default_options() {
        return TransactionOptions{false, false};
    }
};
```

`TransactionOptions` holds `dry_run` (line 12). Note that `default_options()` (lines 15-17) always constructs `{false, false}` — i.e. a struct where `dry_run` is hardcoded to `false`, regardless of what the caller actually wants.

## 2. Entry point — "standard user channel"

**File:** `src/service/user_service.h` (lines 8-16) — declares `UserService`, the standard-channel entry point for user-triggered transactions:

```cpp
class UserService {
public:
    explicit UserService(TransactionManager& tx_manager) : tx_manager_(tx_manager) {}
    void process_transaction(const std::string& user_id, const model::Transaction& tx, bool dry_run);
private:
    TransactionManager& tx_manager_;
};
```

This is exercised by `test_004.cpp` (line 18): `user_service.process_transaction("usr_123", tx, true);` — i.e. a caller explicitly requests `dry_run = true` through the standard `UserService` channel.

## 3/4. Full call chain and where the flag is dropped

**File:** `src/service/user_service.cpp` (lines 5-10) — **this is where the bug is:**

```cpp
void UserService::process_transaction(const std::string& user_id, const model::Transaction& tx, bool dry_run) {
    // BUG: Options struct is populated using default settings but forgets to assign the dry_run parameter.
    // It should perform: options.dry_run = dry_run;
    model::TransactionOptions options = model::TransactionOptions::default_options();
    tx_manager_.execute(tx, options);
}
```

- `process_transaction` receives the caller's `dry_run` argument (e.g. `true`) as a plain `bool` parameter.
- Instead of building `options` from that parameter, it calls `model::TransactionOptions::default_options()` (line 8), which unconditionally returns `dry_run = false` (per `transaction.h` line 16).
- The incoming `dry_run` parameter is **never read/assigned** anywhere in this function — it's effectively a dead parameter.
- The resulting `options` (always `dry_run = false`) is forwarded to `tx_manager_.execute(tx, options)` at line 9.

This is the exact point where the flag is lost: a default-constructed options object is created and used instead of one populated from the real caller-supplied `dry_run` value.

Downstream from there, the flag (now permanently `false`) is faithfully propagated with no further bugs:

**File:** `src/service/transaction_manager.h` (line 10) declares:
```cpp
void execute(const model::Transaction& tx, const model::TransactionOptions& options);
```

**File:** `src/service/transaction_manager.cpp` (lines 5-7):
```cpp
void TransactionManager::execute(const model::Transaction& tx, const model::TransactionOptions& options) {
    db_.write_transaction(tx, options);
}
```
This correctly forwards the (already-corrupted) `options` by const reference to the database client — no issue here.

## 5. Where the actual DB write/commit decision lives

**File:** `src/db/database_client.h` (lines 18-25):

```cpp
void write_transaction(const model::Transaction& tx, const model::TransactionOptions& options) {
    last_tx_id_ = tx.id;
    last_tx_amount_ = tx.amount;
    last_tx_dry_run_ = options.dry_run;
    if (!options.dry_run) {
        committed_tx_ids_.push_back(tx.id);
    }
}
```

This is the terminal "commit to database" logic (simulated via `committed_tx_ids_` in this fixture). It correctly checks `options.dry_run` and only appends to `committed_tx_ids_` (i.e., "writes"/"commits") when `dry_run` is `false` (line 22). This logic is correct in isolation — since `options.dry_run` is always `false` by the time it arrives here (due to the bug in `user_service.cpp`), every transaction gets committed regardless of what the original caller requested.

## Summary — root cause and fix location

- **Root cause file/line:** `src/service/user_service.cpp:8` — `model::TransactionOptions options = model::TransactionOptions::default_options();` discards the `dry_run` function parameter.
- **Fix:** After constructing `options`, add `options.dry_run = dry_run;` (as the existing code comment on lines 6-7 already notes) before calling `tx_manager_.execute(tx, options);` on line 9.
- Everything downstream (`TransactionManager::execute` in `transaction_manager.cpp`, and `DatabaseClient::write_transaction` in `database_client.h`) correctly propagates and honors whatever `dry_run` value is in the `TransactionOptions` struct it receives — no changes needed there.
- Test `test_004.cpp` (lines 8-36) is the regression test that currently fails/would fail against this bug, asserting both that `db.last_tx_dry_run_` is `true` and that `"tx_789"` is absent from `db.committed_tx_ids_`.

Note: I also noticed an unrelated, similarly-patterned bug in `src/service/order_service.cpp` (lines 10-13) where an `empty_context` is substituted for the real `context` when calling `db_.save_order`, causing `correlation_id`/`request_id` to be lost (covered by `test_003.cpp`). This is a different propagation bug (context, not dry-run) — flagging it for awareness, but it's outside the scope of the dry-run investigation you asked for.</result>

Confirmed: both dry-run and normal (committing) transactions behave correctly now.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `src/service/user_service.cpp:5-9` — `UserService::process_transaction` accepted a `dry_run` parameter but never assigned it onto the `TransactionOptions` it built, instead using `TransactionOptions::default_options()` verbatim (which hardcodes `dry_run = false`). That mismatched options object was then forwarded through `TransactionManager::execute` → `DatabaseClient::write_transaction`, both of which correctly propagate/honor `dry_run` — so every user-triggered transaction looked like a non-dry-run and got permanently committed.

**Fix:** added `options.dry_run = dry_run;` before forwarding to `tx_manager_.execute(...)`.

**Verified:**
- `validate_004.py` (dry-run regression test) — now passes (`OK`).
- Manual check with `dry_run = false` — transaction is still committed to `committed_tx_ids_` as expected.
- `validate_003.py` still fails, but that's an unrelated, pre-existing bug in `order_service.cpp` (correlation ID/context propagation), untouched by this change.
